title: Strange sails off Pasai
body:
Shahbandar, a pepper boat from Pasai came in before dawn, low in the water and quick.

Expected in port: the Pasai pepper boat; a junk from Gresik with nutmeg and mace from Banda; a Kling ship from Pulicat with cloth; and the Zhangzhou junk, back from Kedah with more pepper and ready to sail.

Tides: the Zhangzhou junk sails at noon. The Pasai boat wants to sell and be away by evening.

Market: the Banda spices draw every buyer in port. Mace is worth many times its weight in nutmeg, so expect hard bargaining at the scales.

News: the Pasai nakhoda says ships of a kind he has never seen called at Pedir and Pasai, five of them, with guns along their sides. Their men set up a stone cross on the shore and asked questions about the China junks and about Melaka's harbour. He swears to it. The Gujaratis already say these are the same Franks.

Warning: rumours make captains nervous. Some may want to finish their trade quickly and go.
notes: The player is a shahbandar; port-wide berthing and inspection authority is a game abstraction; customs rulings are made in the temenggung's name.

Sequeira's five ships calling at Pedir and Pasai and erecting padroes before reaching Melaka (1509): docs/research/1511-events.md section 1, Gameplay Hook: pre-arrival intelligence. Mace to nutmeg value ratio (Pires): commodities.md section 6. Nutmeg returning from Banda on the east winds: commodities.md.
Ships, people and incidents are fictional. Tide times are game schedule times, not tidal data.
